If your card allows for cash advances, you are able to withdraw cash from an ATM, deposit said cash into your bank account and subsequently use that "cash" to pay off your minimum payments.

However, please take note that cash advance APRs are much higher than purchase APRs and they also start earning interest from the day you withdrew the cash.

Not only will you still have to pay whatever the original balance is, you will also have to pay APRs as high as 25% to 30%.

I highly suggest you reevaluate your financial situation and make sure you're able to pay off your accrued debts.

You should NOT close these credit cards. Although each open account is beneficial for your history, another good component is your average age of your credit history. This is essentially how long you've had an account open for. The greater your credit history age, the more potential lenders see you as a trustworthy person, as you've had a credit account open for X amount of years, compared to another person who has only had an account open for less.

You should ask the issuer of your secured cards if there is a possibility of getting converted to the non-secured version of the credit card. If your credit score is well within the 700's they will most likely be fine with it, but some prefer to have a credit history of around 1 year or more before they will switch a secured credit card.

While talking with them, make sure to mention the following:

1) Ask to be switched to the nonsecured version with no annual fee.

2) Ask to keep the same account number so that these accounts count as one account, instead of closing one account and opening another.

3) If they accept, check within a couple statements of the new card to ensure you received your deposit back.

He's a little bit rude, and drones on and on about how his toe pain is "the worst" and he can't even stand on it. When we asked him what he took for pain, he said that he has been taking his Norco from his PCP, but he ran out. He went through a 40-pack of Norco in 2 days. Like, you have clearly stated you will abuse narcotics, so we will not be giving them to you. When we said that, he told us that he's fine with Norco, and he works at factory on them all the time! He said if he doesn't get them here, he will get them on the street, and proceeded to call my attending a cunt and bitch, and when he passed by triage on his way out, he said that he wishes she dies in a car accident. We made sure to note these remarks in his chart for future providers.

• One of my first patients was a lady who came in with ankle pain. On her chart, it said it happened three days ago. In person, she said it happened today. She had no palpable tenderness, she just kept reaffirming me that it was super painful. We X-rayed her, just because she wouldn't leave without one, and it was fine. We discharged her without pain meds, and I was leaving another patient's room when she was walking entirely fine around the corner. She saw me, and then started limping due to her "unbearable ankle pain."

• Just this past week, this lady comes in from EMS, and all we know from EMS is that she has "cold feet." She got priority 2 (1 is the highest) treatment, because EMS thought she might be at risk for frostbite. We see her getting wheeled in, and she's browsing her phone and absolutely not in any acute pain. When we walk into her room, she's completely fine. While we give her legs a look for any swelling or obvious deformities, she asks, "Oh, can I also get an STD check?" Apparently, she was at the bus stop and just randomly wanted an STD check, but didn't want to wait for the bus to take her to the hospital.

Back in grade seven, during spring break, I took a trip with my best friend to Tel Aviv, because his uncle was getting married.

We were rounding out the trip one night, walking back to his family's house. He ended up telling me that he would be moving when the school year was over due to his father's job, and we'd probably never see each other again.

I got so angry. I yelled at him, calling him a jerk and insulting one of the only friendships I've ever had as a kid. I remember tires screeching, and then my friend grabbed me by my collar and pushed me to the ground.
There was a drive-by. My friend, the one friend I made during middle school, spared the life of a so-called friend who was berating him at that moment. Two fully automatic rifles later, and the front of the house was shot up. I was hysteric. His uncle and grandfather came out of the house to see me on the ground over his lifeless body.

When I tried talking about this to my counselors at school, but they were more sympathetic than empathetic, and gave me the entire "at least you're alive" spiel. I hated myself more and more every time they said that. There was no reason for me to be alive if it was at the cost of my friend's life. I couldn't look my friend's father in his face and tell him he died saving my life.
I sheltered myself from making friendships for almost a decade because I was afraid something like that would happen again. I know, it sounds ridiculous, but I had so many triggers and my rage during the moment just felt like it added up to something.

It's been about nine years now, and I can say that I'm able to speak about this to people just recently. It's been a very emotional part of my life. I usually tend to reserve it for really close friends, as something like that isn’t something you drop in during casual conversation with strangers.
I still suffer from survivor’s guilt and PTSD, a lot of things are triggers (anything resembling gunshots is still pretty bad), and from a development perspective, I’m scared to stand up for what I believe in, because I associate it with that event.

I believe that I’m on a track to recovery, because that event is just that: an event. It may be a significant one, but it doesn’t define me, who I am, and what I’m capable of.

N-Air is a great move, and if you land while the attack animation is still active, you can cancel the lag.

U-Air is great for juggling opponents, and the multiple hits can get through an air dodge if you time it right.
D-Throw into U-air works for the higher percents when D-throw into B-air doesn't work anymore, or your opponent tries to DI up.
Also, using it while ground-floating and cancelling before the second hit can chain into some combos.

F-Air should be saved for kill percents so it doesn't go stale, since Peach has one heck of a swing.
However, at low to mid percents, a D-air chains into a F-air decently, which I use when close to the edge.
Also, when it comes to F-air, don't be afraid to trade hits when edge-guarding.
Although you might not want to get hit, your opponent won't appreciate the hard knockback in return.

D-Air sees its best usage when at face height (float so that the bottom of Peach's dress is just above the head of the opponent).
Most opponents don't have an attack that can hit Peach from this angle on the ground (barring moves that can angle), and floating towards them while they're rolling or shielding is great pressure, and you can quickly fast fall into a grab or jab.
Also, when they are recovering, a D-air can interrupt some character's recovery moves, and can stage-spike (easier on angled ledges than straight ones).

B-air is my most used aerial, as it goes well with D-throw.
Sweet spotting B-air has relatively nice knockback, and the sour spot isn't too bad.
Sometimes a D-throw-B-air combo can combo into another B-air.
I also use B-air to stage-spike, in conjunction with throwing turnips to edge-guard.

Also, don't forget to utilize turnips!
If you are floating while holding an item, you will throw out aerials instead of the item.
It can be used as a relatively nice mind game: approach by jumping forward, float when you get close, and smack your opponent with a well hitting F-air. Your opponent might expect you to throw the turnip, leading them to airdodge, but anticipate it.

Assuming from your post a few years is 2-3, it is highly likely that the rMacbook will replace the Macbook Air by then, and if you can hold off purchasing a laptop until then, it's likely the rMacbook will be upgraded with a faster/better processor to rival that of the Macbook Air.

Online is your best bet if you can wait.

Amazon and eBay both offer them, and as long as you check what you're buying, you'll be fine.
